item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-565f4c36128a2a84","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh reported that constitutional fundamental rights were enforceable through the courts, that an aggrieved person could petition the Supreme Court, and that courts increasingly considered international human-rights law; however, implementation of ICCPR provisions generally required enabling legislation and could not be achieved through one statute alone.","question_ids":["3B.4","4B.4","4B.10","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Primarily historical and institutional context predating 2023; no direct 2023 outcome evidence.","ruler_attribution":"Institutional claims concern the Bangladesh government and courts during Sheikh Hasina's tenure; direct personal attribution to Hasina is limited.","limitations":["Government self-report; claims are not independently verified in these units."]},{"source_id":"SRC-565f4c36128a2a84","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh reported constitutional equality protections for religion, race, caste, sex, and birthplace; disability legislation prohibited discrimination in education and public access; and the government had drafted an anti-discrimination bill that remained under consideration.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","6B.3","6B.8","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Historical policy and legal measures, mostly predating 2023; not evidence of 2023 implementation or outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"Government policy and legislation during Hasina's administration; no specific personal directive is identified.","limitations":["Self-reported legal framework; practical enforcement and incidence are not established."]},{"source_id":"SRC-565f4c36128a2a84","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh described an extensive anti-child-marriage and anti-dowry program involving laws, local prevention committees, awareness activities, school stipends and meals, adolescent clubs, birth and marriage registration, a helpline, stakeholder consultations, and training in 480 upazilas.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Historical program evidence predating 2023; durability and 2023 results are not shown.","ruler_attribution":"Government program under Hasina's administration; personal direction by Hasina is not specified.","limitations":["Government-reported activities and outputs; effectiveness and distributional outcomes are not independently assessed."]},{"source_id":"SRC-565f4c36128a2a84","start_unit":10,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh reported that law-enforcement personnel were subject to criminal, legal, and disciplinary proceedings for abuses; more than 2,516 RAB members had allegedly faced imprisonment, dismissal, or removal from service for offenses and human-rights violations.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","4B.4","7B.2","7B.7","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Historical government-reported accountability record, not limited to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Government and law-enforcement institutional practice during Hasina's tenure; no direct personal order is stated.","limitations":["Self-reported aggregate figure; cases, standards, and completeness cannot be verified from the supplied units."]},{"source_id":"SRC-565f4c36128a2a84","start_unit":27,"end_unit":31,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh reported prison safeguards including investigations of deaths, disciplinary action for responsible personnel, prison medical facilities and specialist appointments, CCTV monitoring, complaint mechanisms, separation of juveniles, and legal requirements for prompt presentation before magistrates; it also acknowledged that it lacked facilities for prisoner rehabilitation because of financial and logistical constraints.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","6B.2","6B.6","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Historical institutional evidence predating 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Government-reported prison administration; direct personal responsibility of Hasina is not established.","limitations":["Includes government assertions and an explicit capacity limitation; no 2023 verification."]},{"source_id":"SRC-565f4c36128a2a84","start_unit":32,"end_unit":34,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh reported domestic-violence and anti-trafficking laws, monitoring cells, police and victim-support desks, shelters, data systems, police training, and local committees; it also reported substantial rescues and prosecutions, while acknowledging that trafficking and child labor persisted and that enforcement remained an ongoing programmatic task.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Historical program evidence, largely before 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Government institutions under Hasina's administration; personal attribution is not specified.","limitations":["Government-reported outputs; persistence of harms limits inference about effectiveness."]},{"source_id":"SRC-565f4c36128a2a84","start_unit":37,"end_unit":40,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh described legal limits and judicial review for preventive detention, including 30-day orders, a six-month constitutional limit absent Advisory Board review, Supreme Court directives, and a requirement to report ICCPR implementation; it also acknowledged lack of prisoner rehabilitation facilities.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","7B.2","7B.7","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Historical legal framework predating 2023; does not establish 2023 compliance.","ruler_attribution":"Government and judiciary during Hasina's tenure; no direct personal decision is identified.","limitations":["Formal safeguards do not demonstrate actual compliance; source is a state report."]},{"source_id":"SRC-565f4c36128a2a84","start_unit":42,"end_unit":43,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh reported electoral participation in local elections by major parties with substantial turnout, and stated that a new Election Commission was formed after consultations with political parties and a civil-society-inclusive search committee.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.4","4B.7","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Historical electoral evidence, mainly 2014–2016, not direct evidence for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Reported government and presidential electoral administration; Hasina's direct role is not specified.","limitations":["Does not address the quality of national elections during 2023 or opposition access."]},{"source_id":"SRC-565f4c36128a2a84","start_unit":47,"end_unit":47,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh stated that it would continue ICCPR reporting and seek broader civil-society participation in future reports.","question_ids":["3B.4","4B.3","4B.6","5B.7","6B.5","7B.2","7B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Forward-looking institutional commitment from a historical report; no evidence of 2023 completion.","ruler_attribution":"Government commitment during Hasina's administration; personal authorship is not shown.","limitations":["Commitment is not evidence of implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-576a5afb7b4d817d","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported that Bangladesh recovered rapidly from COVID-19 with prudent macroeconomic policies, but in 2023 faced inflation, energy shortages, a $7.2 billion first-half FY23 balance-of-payments deficit, revenue shortfalls, bank liquidity and non-performing-loan challenges, and growth projected at 5.2 percent in FY23; it recommended trade reform, export diversification, a market-based exchange rate, and stronger resilience.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly relevant to 2023, with FY23 data and contemporaneous assessment.","ruler_attribution":"Country-level assessment of Bangladesh during Hasina's government; it does not attribute each policy personally to Hasina.","limitations":["Recommendations and macro indicators do not establish causal responsibility or distributional outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-62e6a780a2f956c9","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Fortify Rights reported that under Hasina's government Rohingya refugees faced years of militant killings, abductions, torture, and threats in Bangladesh; reported killings by camp-based militants rose from 42 in 2022 to 90 in 2023, and the organization alleged that government refusal to publicly acknowledge militant groups impeded justice and appropriate responses.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.6","6B.10","7B.2","8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The reported 90 killings directly cover 2023, while the assessment was published in 2025 and describes a longer period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the alleged failure to the Hasina government; it does not establish a specific personal order by Hasina.","limitations":["Secondary report summarizing Fortify Rights; government response and full causal attribution are not supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8c84a8a4fee63ace","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Transparency International stated that the 2023 CPI found corruption thriving globally, with weakening justice systems reducing accountability and political interference enabling impunity; it specifically characterized Asia Pacific as stagnant for five years because governments failed to deliver anti-corruption commitments.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Regional 2023 assessment; the supplied units do not provide Bangladesh's country score or a Hasina-specific finding.","ruler_attribution":"No direct attribution to Hasina or Bangladesh in the supplied units.","limitations":["Regional and global claims cannot by themselves establish Bangladesh-specific or ruler-specific facts."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4814b424f641d956","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported that in FY2023 Bangladesh's growth slowed to 5.8 percent; inflation reduced purchasing power especially for poor people; the balance-of-payments deficit widened to $8.2 billion; import controls caused shortages; and the gross non-performing-loan ratio rose to 9 percent in December 2023 from 8.2 percent in December 2022. It also noted government adjustments including fuel-price reform, reduced export subsidies, and a Prompt Corrective Action framework.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly relevant to FY2023 and December 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Country-level assessment of policies under Hasina's government; personal responsibility is not separately established.","limitations":["The report records both reforms and adverse outcomes; it does not determine whether the reforms caused the outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2968e5cdf14600d7","start_unit":13,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that ahead of the January 2024 election, Bangladesh authorities targeted opposition leaders and supporters; nearly 10,000 opposition activists had been arrested since October 28, at least 16 people were killed, more than 5,500 injured, and security forces were implicated in excessive force, mass arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances, torture, and extrajudicial killings. HRW also reported that Hasina urged supporters to respond to arson with reciprocal burning and that police and Awami League activists coordinated in targeting opposition activists.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.3","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.8","4B.9","4B.10","7B.1","7B.2","7B.8","7B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers October–November 2023, immediately before the scheduled January 2024 election.","ruler_attribution":"HRW directly attributes the retaliatory statement to Hasina and broader conduct to Bangladesh authorities and senior government leaders.","limitations":["HRW relied on interviews, videos, and police reports; the supplied units also note violence by multiple sides."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2968e5cdf14600d7","start_unit":17,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"HRW reported that police used tear gas, sound grenades, rubber bullets, kicking, beating, and dragging against October 28 protesters; opposition members faced mass arrests, allegedly fabricated cases, incommunicado detention, enforced disappearance, and torture, including electric shocks, while authorities sealed BNP offices and refused to disclose some detainees' whereabouts.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.2","4B.3","4B.9","7B.2","7B.7","7B.10","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly relevant to election-related repression in late 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Conduct is attributed to police, authorities, and aligned actors; Hasina's direct operational involvement is not established in these units.","limitations":["Evidence is based on witness accounts, videos, media, and police reports; allegations are not adjudicated here."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0e4b7bea1f80dcae","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Freedom House rated Bangladesh Partly Free at 40/100 and reported that the Awami League consolidated power through harassment of opposition, critical media, and civil society; corruption was endemic, anticorruption enforcement politicized, due process weak, security forces operated with near impunity, and violence against minorities and Rohingya refugees remained significant. It also reported that the 2018 election was delegitimized by violence, fraud allegations, and exclusion of monitors.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.10","7B.6","7B.10","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2023 country assessment, with some findings describing the preceding period and 2018 election.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes consolidation to the Awami League government led by Sheikh Hasina.","limitations":["Aggregate country assessment; not all findings are specific to 2023 or to Hasina personally."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0e4b7bea1f80dcae","start_unit":5,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"Freedom House reported that opposition parties faced harassment, arrests, disrupted rallies, weak electoral prospects, politicized election administration and judiciary, endemic corruption, pressure on media and NGOs, the Digital Security Act's warrantless search and arrest powers, surveillance and censorship, excessive force against protests, and political influence over academic and civic institutions.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.8","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","4B.10","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2023 assessment based mainly on 2022 and earlier conditions; relevant as inherited context for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Findings concern the Awami League government and institutions under Hasina's rule.","limitations":["Some evidence predates 2023; country-report scoring is not reproduced as a ruler score."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fe3434758dcdcc16","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch documented enforced disappearances, torture, extrajudicial killings, arbitrary arrests, surveillance, and denial of accountability during Hasina's decade-long rule; it reported that disappearances increased sharply before elections, opposition activists were targeted, and authorities generally denied allegations and failed to investigate or punish perpetrators.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","4B.10","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Historical evidence through 2021; relevant to inherited institutional conditions but not direct 2023 evidence.","ruler_attribution":"HRW links the pattern to the Awami League government led by Hasina and to security forces under its authority.","limitations":["The report predates 2023 and relies on documented cases, interviews, and secondary sources; it does not establish every 2023 event."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fe3434758dcdcc16","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"HRW reported that government surveillance capacity was used against critics, including through the Digital Security Act and COVID-related monitoring units; it described arrests, alleged secret detention and torture, and the use of dual-use interception and social-media monitoring technologies to control undesirable views.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Evidence through 2021; provides historical institutional context for 2023 digital-control questions.","ruler_attribution":"HRW attributes the surveillance program to the government under Hasina.","limitations":["Historical evidence predating 2023; specific 2023 use and Hasina's personal authorization are not shown."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fe3434758dcdcc16","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"HRW reported that police officers implicated in repression and alleged abuses received awards and promotions, including the promotion of a former RAB commander associated with extrajudicial executions and enforced disappearances to inspector general of police; it characterized accountability as exceptional rather than routine.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","4B.5","7B.5","7B.9","7B.10","8B.4","8B.5","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Historical evidence through 2021; relevant to institutional personnel incentives entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes promotion and award practices to the Hasina-led government and security hierarchy.","limitations":["Evidence is historical and includes allegations; it does not establish the decision-maker for every appointment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fe3434758dcdcc16","start_unit":23,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"HRW reported that formal safeguards against torture and unlawful detention existed, including the Torture and Custodial Death Act and Supreme Court arrest guidelines, but legal-immunity provisions, military jurisdiction, opaque internal tribunals, and government sanctions requirements impeded prosecution of security-force abuses.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Historical legal and institutional evidence through 2021; not direct 2023 implementation evidence.","ruler_attribution":"Legal framework and enforcement environment existed under Hasina's government; direct personal responsibility is not established.","limitations":["The report identifies both formal safeguards and structural barriers; practical 2023 operation is not shown."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ee49de4eccb60463","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Amnesty's supplied 2025 report states that the Cyber Security Act of 2023, enacted under the former government, was used against critics in ways contravening freedom of expression; it also reports later UN findings that the former government and its security apparatus systematically committed serious violations during 2024 and that leaked audio allegedly indicated Hasina authorized lethal force.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.10","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The Cyber Security Act fact concerns 2023; the lethal-force and systematic-violation findings concern 2024 and are outside the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the 2023 law to the former Hasina government; later allegations concern Hasina personally.","limitations":["Most supplied material is about 2024–2025, not 2023; later findings cannot be treated as 2023 facts."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-08b96201d41ab3fa","SRC-249d9fc631b975e0","SRC-c63b4981c9fd56ac"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus is heterogeneous in date: several documents provide historical or later retrospective evidence rather than direct observations from 2023.","The corpus contains government self-reporting, country assessments, rights investigations, and macroeconomic reporting; facts are preserved without resolving source disagreements or scoring the ruler.","The World Bank ISR page supplied only navigation and metadata blocks, with no substantive project evidence relevant to the questions."]}
